summary:
Fully resolved the menu-cursor highlight render path. Starting from wbase 0x27BD (and ~95 sibling call sites across all overlays), the thunk 0xDF85 resolves to wroot IMAGE offset 0x24E9 = wroot FILE offset 0x26E9 = a string-printer wrapper. The wrapper loops over the null-terminated string and per-character calls wroot file 0x24B7 (= image 0x22B7) — the per-char HIGHLIGHT renderer. That function stores the cell as (char_byte, attr<<4) and dispatches via [cs:0x1b8a] (ega.drv slot 1) for the 1bpp wfont0-based per-plane-selector blit. Slot 1 is at ega.drv file 0x19A. Its per-pixel formula yields foreground=palette_index_0, background=palette_index_attr_low_nibble. For the menu-cursor case (df85 called with attr=-5; absolute value 5 stored), the rendered pixels are (color_attr_0) for stroke and (color_attr_5) for background.

The KEY CORRECTION over the prior findings: the live VGA AC palette (NOT the DAC) IS programmed to WIZ6_MAIN in every captured save. WIZ6_MAIN at wroot file 0x2043 is a 16-byte AC palette register table (+1 overscan byte), not a DAC table. It remaps color_attr -> DAC_index as: [0x00, 0x17, 0x11, 0x15, 0x14, 0x16, 0x12, 0x13, 0x10, 0x07, 0x01, 0x05, 0x04, 0x06, 0x02, 0x03]. The DAC itself stays in BIOS default shape (entries 0-15 = standard EGA, 16-23 = high-intensity variants of 0-7). For attr=5: AC[5] = 0x16 -> DAC[22] = (255, 255, 85) = YELLOW. For attr=0: AC[0] = 0x00 -> DAC[0] = (0, 0, 0) = BLACK. The menu cursor renders BLACK ON YELLOW — matching the user's empirical observation exactly.

The prior finding wfont-highlight-render.json had the call path, cell encoding, and per-pixel slot-1 formula correct. It got TWO things wrong: (1) it labeled the per-char function offset as 0x22B7 'file_offset' when 0x22B7 is the IMAGE offset (file offset is 0x24B7); (2) it interpreted WIZ6_MAIN.ts as direct RGB values for the DAC instead of as AC palette register indices, leading to the wrong final color claim of (170, 255, 0) yellow-green. The wfont-highlight-render.json also missed that the actual thunk target 0xDF85 is a string-printer WRAPPER at image 0x24E9 above the per-char function. The prior finding state4-runtime-palette.json incorrectly concluded that WIZ6_MAIN is 'never the active DAC in any captured save' — that's true but trivially so because WIZ6_MAIN writes to the AC palette, not the DAC. WIZ6_MAIN is in fact active in every save state.

verified_call_sites.summary: Scanned every .ovr for E8 near-calls landing on thunks 0xDF81 / 0xDF85 / 0xDF89. Found 0 calls to 0xDF81 or 0xDF89. Found 95+ calls to 0xDF85 across wbase (11), wdopt (8), wmaze (15), wmele (5), wmexe (3), wmnpc (22), wpcmk (11), wpcvw (56), wpops (15), wtrea (19). EVERY overlay call is to 0xDF85. The 0xDF81 hypothesis in the task description was wrong — there is no near-by sibling thunk; all sites use the SAME thunk.

thunk_delta_law_clarification.claim: The thunk-delta law as stated in CLAUDE.md ('thunk_address = wroot_file_offset + 0xBA9C') is misleading. It is actually 'thunk_address = wroot_IMAGE_offset + 0xBA9C'. To get the wroot FILE offset, add 0x200 (the MZ header size). The prior wfont-highlight-render.json finding labeled image offsets as 'file_offset' which is the source of the apparent 0x232 discrepancy.
thunk_delta_law_clarification.verification: ui_window_create example from CLAUDE.md: thunk 0xBBB6 - 0xBA9C = 0x011A. At file 0x011A in wroot.exe we find all-zero bytes (the MZ header). At file 0x031A (= 0x011A + 0x200) we find a function prologue 55 8b ec - that IS ui_window_create. So the thunk-delta-law result is an IMAGE offset, not a file offset.
thunk_delta_law_clarification.rule_of_thumb: When citing wroot offsets from the thunk-delta law, BE EXPLICIT: thunk - 0xBA9C is the IMAGE offset. To grep bytes in original/wroot.exe, add 0x200.

df85_target_resolution.signature: void render_highlight_string(uint16_t window_handle, char* str, int16_t attr)

per_char_function.name: ui_window_putchar_highlight
per_char_function.signature: void render_highlight_char(uint16_t window_handle, uint16_t char_word, int16_t attr)
per_char_function.behavior: Walks the window list at cs:0x1bd2 to find a matching handle; if found, computes (char, attr_byte) cell where attr_byte = (|attr| & 0x0F) << 4. Stores into the window's cell array at [bx+si+0x10]. Reads/updates the dirty-map byte at [cs:0x1b60]:cell_offset. If the dirty-map byte's low 6 bits match the window index, calls ega.drv slot 1 via [cs:0x1b8a] to render the cell pixels. The 'negated_flag' (= sign-bit of input attr) is OR'd as bit 7 into the dirty-map byte but does NOT affect rendered pixels — it's a marker bit consumed by upstream cursor-tracking logic.
asm_excerpts: 0x24CE  f6 c4 80       test ah, 0x80        ; sign bit?
0x24DD..0x24FE  ; walk window list to find matching handle, dl = window_index
0x2511  8a e0          mov ah, al           ; ah = low byte of attr
0x2513  b1 04 d2 e4    mov cl, 4; shl ah, cl ; ah = (attr & 0xFF) << 4
0x251D  89 46 fe       mov [bp-2], ax       ; save cell word
0x254C  24 3f          and al, 0x3f         ; mask to 6-bit window index
0x254E  3a c2          cmp al, dl           ; matches our window?
0x2558  0c 80          or al, 0x80          ; set bit 7 if negated
0x255A  8a 25          mov ah, [di]         ; ah = original dirty byte
0x255D  88 05          mov [di], al         ; write modified dirty byte back
0x25A8  8b f8          mov di, ax           ; di = back-buffer dest offset
0x25AA  8b 46 fe       mov ax, [bp-2]       ; ax = cell word
0x25AD  ff 76 fa       push word [bp-6]     ; -> slot-1 [bp+6] (negated_flag, unused by slot 1)
per_char_function.cell_encoding: Each visible window cell stores 2 bytes: low byte = char code (0..127), high byte = (|attr| & 0x0F) << 4. The fact that the low nibble of the high byte is 0 is the blit-time signal to route the cell to slot 1 (highlight) instead of slot 2 (normal text). See blit_dispatch below.

slot_dispatch_table.structure: Slot table is N 4-byte entries (offset:segment far pointers). Loaded by driver loader (wroot image 0x1F76+) which patches each entry's segment word at startup.

known_slots.purpose: 1bpp text + highlight render (per-plane bit selector). Called by per-char highlight fn (0x24B7) and by the per-cell blit loop (wroot image 0x2A20-area) for any cell whose attr_byte low nibble is 0.
4bpp text render (normal text). Called by per-char normal fn (wroot image 0x23E3 = file 0x25E3) and by the per-cell blit loop for cells with attr_byte low nibble in 1..4 (font selector 1..4).

ega_drv_slot_1.name: ega_drv_slot1_text_1bpp_per_plane_selector
ega_drv_slot_1.purpose: Renders one 8x8 cell using wfont0 as a 1bpp glyph mask, OR all-zeros, on a per-plane basis. The 4 EGA planes are written independently. For each plane P in 0..3, the plane's source is selected by bit (4+P) of ah: if set, source is wfont0[char*8] (the 1bpp glyph); if clear, source is a fixed 8-byte zero buffer at ega.drv file 0x192. After source selection, the plane writes are OPTIONALLY NOT-inverted based on word [bp+8] (the dirty-map byte from the caller — always non-zero on real call paths).

args.al: char code (used to index wfont0 at char*8)
args.ah: attr-byte from cell: original attr in HIGH nibble (bits 4-7), low nibble = 0
args.[bp+6]: ignored (the per-char fn pushes the negated_flag here; slot 1 never reads it)
args.[bp+8]: WORD: when non-zero, plane writes are NOT-inverted; when zero, plain copy. In practice ALWAYS non-zero (it's the dirty-map byte with low 6 bits = window index that just matched).
args.[bp+0xA]: segment-like word. (dh & 0x40) -> alt branch at 0x380 (not used on normal call paths).

per_plane_loop_template: mov dx, 0x3C4; mov al, 2; out dx, al    ; SEQ index 2 (map mask)
inc dx; mov al, 1<<P; out dx, al        ; map_mask = bit-P-only
test ah, 0x10<
lds si, [bp-8]                         ; CLEAR: use 8-byte zero buffer
jmp PLAIN_COPY                         ;        (zero buffer, NO inversion check)
movsb; add di, cx                      ; 8x: raw byte to plane
lodsb; not al; stosb; add di, cx       ; 8x: NOT byte to plane
ega_drv_slot_1.color_formula:
Let attr_lo = (cell_attr_byte >> 4) & 0x0F = the original |attr| value held in the high nibble. Let w(x,y) = wfont0[char*8 + y] bit (7-x), the 1bpp glyph mask. Let invert = ([bp+8] != 0) which is ALWAYS true on real call paths.

For each pixel (x, y) in 0..7:
  plane_bit_P = (attr_lo & (1<<P)) ? (invert ? !w(x,y) : w(x,y)) : 0
  color_attr_at_pixel = sum(plane_bit_P << P for P in 0..3)

With invert=true (the only observed case):
  if w(x,y) == 1 (stroke):     color_attr = 0
  if w(x,y) == 0 (background): color_attr = attr_lo

Final rendered RGB = DAC[AC[color_attr]] where AC is the live attribute-controller palette and DAC is the VGA DAC.

runtime_palette_state.claim: The WIZ6_MAIN palette IS active in every captured save state — it is loaded as the AC palette (attribute controller registers 0..15), NOT as the DAC (digital-to-analog converter entries 0..255). The DAC stays in BIOS default shape with entries 0-15 = standard EGA colors and entries 16-23 = high-intensity variants.

trace: 1. df85 = thunk 0xDF85 -> wroot image 0x24E9 / file 0x26E9 (string wrapper).
2. Wrapper loops over str, per-char calls wroot image 0x22B7 / file 0x24B7 with (window, char_byte, attr=-5).
3. Per-char fn detects sign bit of attr; sets negated_flag=1; negates ax -> |attr|=5.
4. Stores cell = (char, 5<<4 = 0x50). Low nibble of attr_byte is 0 -> blit-time dispatch routes via [cs:0x1b8a] = ega.drv slot 1.
6. Per-plane test: ah & 0x10 -> P0 = NOT(wfont0); ah & 0x20 = 0 -> P1 = zero; ah & 0x40 -> P2 = NOT(wfont0); ah & 0x80 = 0 -> P3 = zero.
7. Pixel where wfont0_bit = 1: all planes = NOT(1) = 0 -> color_attr 0.
8. Pixel where wfont0_bit = 0: P0 = NOT(0) = 1, P1 = 0, P2 = NOT(0) = 1, P3 = 0 -> color_attr = 0b0101 = 5.

result.visual: Black-on-yellow — MATCHES user's empirical observation of selected menu rows.

wfont_highlight_render_json.actual_truth: 0x22B7 is the IMAGE offset (= file 0x24B7). The thunk 0xDF85 actually resolves to wroot IMAGE 0x24E9 / FILE 0x26E9, which is a string-printer WRAPPER. The wrapper calls the per-char fn at image 0x22B7 / file 0x24B7 in a loop. So the prior finding documented the per-char function correctly but missed the wrapper above it, and confused image vs. file offsets throughout.
wfont_highlight_render_json.severity: moderate — fix the offsets and re-label as image-not-file; the asm trace itself is correct

wfont_highlight_render_json.what_it_said: palette[5] = (170, 255, 0) yellow-green via WIZ6_MAIN matches the user's observation
wfont_highlight_render_json.actual_truth: WIZ6_MAIN.ts mis-encodes the palette: it stored AC palette register VALUES as if they were direct RGB triples. The actual semantics: WIZ6_MAIN[5] = AC register value 0x16 = DAC index 22. Under the live VGA default DAC, DAC[22] = (255, 255, 85) = YELLOW (not yellow-green). The TS file's claim of (170, 255, 0) yellow-green is wrong; (255, 255, 85) yellow is correct.
wfont_highlight_render_json.severity: high — produces visually wrong output if used as-is

wfont_highlight_render_json.what_it_said: highlight cells render as 'wfont0 glyph in palette-0 (black) on a palette-attr background'
wfont_highlight_render_json.actual_truth: Correct in structure. The stroke is color_attr 0 and the background is color_attr |input_attr|. Looking those up through the live AC and DAC: stroke=DAC[AC[0]]=DAC[0]=BLACK; background=DAC[AC[attr]]. This part of the prior finding is RIGHT — it was just the WIZ6_MAIN.ts data file that was wrong.

state4_runtime_palette_json.what_it_said: WIZ6_MAIN is never the active DAC in any captured save
state4_runtime_palette_json.actual_truth: Technically true (WIZ6_MAIN doesn't write to the DAC), but MISLEADING. WIZ6_MAIN is loaded into the AC palette registers — those ARE active in every save. The finding's conclusion 'render against EGA_DEFAULT and the colors will match' is WRONG: the colors won't match because the AC palette remaps every attribute index 0..15 to different DAC indices, including indices 16..23 which produce high-intensity colors not in the EGA_DEFAULT table.
state4_runtime_palette_json.severity: high — the finding's recommended action (use EGA_DEFAULT for rendering) produces visually wrong output

state4_runtime_palette_json.actual_truth: Under EGA_DEFAULT it would be magenta, but the live AC palette is WIZ6_MAIN. With AC active, attr=5 -> AC[5]=0x16 -> DAC[22] = (255, 255, 85) YELLOW. The 'user's actual reference image' the finding's open_questions mentioned has now been pixel-matched: user sees YELLOW because the AC palette is doing its job.

open_questions.claim: All 13 captured saves have the SAME AC palette = WIZ6_MAIN. Saves cover game_state 1 (title) and 0xFFFF (unknown). State 4 (main menu) was not captured but the AC palette state would carry over from state 2 (winit) where it's loaded once and never reprogrammed. No state-4 save needed for AC palette confirmation.

WIZ6_DUNGEON load site exists at wroot image 0x2105 / file 0x2305 with a similar AC palette table; it may be loaded on state transitions to dungeon (states 5/6/0x17). No dungeon-state saves captured; can't verify.

The negated_flag bit (bit 7) df85 OR's into the dirty-map byte at [cs:0x1b60]:cell_offset has SOME consumer (otherwise df85 wouldn't bother). Candidates: (a) cursor-blink toggle that re-renders the highlighted cell each tick; (b) selection-state read-back when user presses Enter; (c) a 'restore prior cell' undo on cursor-move. Not investigated.
Slot 1 has an alt path at ega.drv 0x380 entered when ([bp+0xA] high byte & 0x40) != 0. Not exercised by df85. May be a 'render to non-EGA target' variant.

implications_for_port: The viewer's font-rendering for highlight cells should use this color formula. Stroke = palette-attr-0; background = palette-attr-|input_attr|. The current `{1:0, 8:14}` override in CastleScreen is an approximation that happens to land on yellow because EGA_DEFAULT[14] also = (255,255,85), but it's brittle: it only works because the 4bpp wfont3 glyphs use file colors 1 and 8, and our viewer's palette[14] happens to be the same color as DAC[22]. The engine-correct implementation: discard the 4bpp wfont3 glyph and use a 1bpp wfont0 mask producing stroke-at-attr-0 vs bg-at-attr-|input_attr|.
packages/data/src/palettes/wiz6-main.ts MUST be corrected. The current RGB triples are wrong. Replace with computed values from WIZ6_MAIN_AC table applied to VGA_DEFAULT_DAC[0..23].

The CastleScreen menu cursor color override should be `{ stroke: attrToRgb(0), background: attrToRgb(5) }` = `{ stroke: [0,0,0], background: [255,255,85] }` (black-on-yellow). NOT EGA_DEFAULT[5] (magenta) and NOT WIZ6_MAIN's incorrectly-encoded palette[5] (yellow-green).

Audit any OTHER findings or code that interpret WIZ6_MAIN.ts as direct RGB triples. The error there is systemic — anywhere we look up WIZ6_MAIN[k] expecting an RGB, we get a small integer (the AC register value). Worth a grep across packages/.
For arbitrary highlight attrs (other overlays use a wide range), the effective_color_table_attr_to_RGB above gives the engine-correct background color. Strokes are always black.
